Merge several VCF files into a gen_tibble

Source: R/gt_merge_vcfs.R
gt_merge_vcfs.Rd

This function reads several VCF files with different samples (e.g. one per population, or per sequencing batch) into a single gen_tibble, as bcftools merge would, followed by gen_tibble(). It is much faster than reading each file with gen_tibble() and merging them with rbind() (one pair at a time), and needs no space on disk beyond the merged gen_tibble: each file is read twice, once for its loci (to match them across files) and once for its genotypes, which are written straight into the merged backing file.

Usage

gt_merge_vcfs(
  files,
  variants = c("intersection", "union"),
  missing_to_ref = FALSE,
  alt_mismatch = c("drop", "split"),
  ref_mismatch = c("error", "drop", "swap"),
  force_samples = FALSE,
  backingfile = NULL,
  valid_alleles = c("A", "T", "C", "G"),
  missing_alleles = c("0", "."),
  allow_duplicates = FALSE,
  names_as_int = TRUE,
  chromosomes_as_int = FALSE,
  n_cores = 1,
  phased = FALSE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

files

a character vector with the paths to two or more VCF files (.vcf or .vcf.gz, which are read faster if compressed with bgzip).

variants

which sites to keep: "intersection" (the default) keeps the sites found in all files; "union" keeps all sites (see details).

missing_to_ref

boolean: with variants = "union", whether the genotypes of the samples of a file at sites that are not in that file are homozygous for the reference allele (as with bcftools merge -0), rather than missing (the default).

alt_mismatch

what to do with loci at the same position that have the same REF but a different ALT allele: "drop" (the default) drops the site, "split" keeps them as separate loci (see details).

ref_mismatch

what to do with loci at the same position that have a different REF allele: "error" (the default) stops with an error, "drop" drops the site, "swap" merges loci whose alleles are swapped, swapping their genotypes (see details).

force_samples

boolean: whether to allow the same sample name in different files, prefixing the duplicated names by the index of their file (see details). Defaults to FALSE.

backingfile

the path, including the file name without extension, for the backing files of the merged gen_tibble (a .bk file for the genotypes, a .rds file for the FBM, and a .gt file for the gen_tibble). If NULL, the path of the first file is used, with "_merged" added to its name (and a version number if those files already exist, as in gen_tibble()).

valid_alleles

a vector of valid allele values; it defaults to 'A','T', 'C' and 'G'.

missing_alleles

a vector of values in the VCF files that are considered as missing alleles ('.' is always missing).

allow_duplicates

boolean: whether to allow duplicated loci (the same chromosome and position) or duplicated loci names in the merged gen_tibble (see gen_tibble()).

names_as_int

boolean: whether the loci names are integers (the index of each locus in the merged gen_tibble) rather than the VCF IDs, which saves memory with many loci (see gen_tibble()). Note that it defaults to TRUE, unlike in gen_tibble() (where it defaults to FALSE): merging VCF files is mostly used for large datasets, in which the loci names take most of the memory of the gen_tibble and are rarely needed (loci are identified by their chromosome and position). Set it to FALSE to keep the VCF IDs. With integer names, the VCF IDs (with the chromosomes and positions) are written to a sidecar file next to the backing file, from which gt_lookup_loci() and gt_restore_loci() get them back.

chromosomes_as_int

boolean: whether the chromosomes are integer codes rather than a factor, which saves memory with many chromosomes (e.g. RAD loci assembled de novo); the names are written to a sidecar file next to the backing file (see gen_tibble() and gt_lookup_chromosomes()). Default is FALSE.

n_cores

the number of cores used to decompress bgzipped files and to parse the genotypes. Defaults to 1.

phased

boolean: whether to store phased genotypes, giving a phased gen_tibble (see phased in gen_tibble()). All the files must then be phased: any unphased genotype (with '/') or individual that is not diploid is an error. Default is FALSE (the phase is ignored, as in gen_tibble()). The alleles of phased genotypes are never swapped (as in rbind()), so ref_mismatch = "swap" is not available.

quiet

boolean: whether to omit the report of the merge.

Value

a gen_tibble with the merged data (saved, as with gen_tibble()).

Details

As with gen_tibble(), only biallelic SNPs are read from each file. Loci are matched across files by chromosome and position (as in bcftools merge), so chromosomes need to be named in the same way in all files (a mix of e.g. 'chr1' and '1' would match no loci). A locus is merged with a site at the same chromosome and position if their alleles agree: the same REF and ALT alleles, or a missing allele (e.g. the ALT '.' of a monomorphic locus), which takes the allele of the other files (a site with the same alleles is preferred to one with a missing allele). Loci whose alleles do not agree are handled as follows:

  • loci with the same REF but a different ALT allele (e.g. A/C and A/G): bcftools merge would make a multiallelic site, which a gen_tibble can not store, so by default the site is dropped (alt_mismatch = "drop"); with alt_mismatch = "split" (as bcftools merge -m none), the loci are kept as separate loci at the same position (which needs allow_duplicates = TRUE), each with missing genotypes for the samples of the other files.

  • loci with a different REF allele (e.g. A/C and C/A): the REF allele should be the base of the reference genome at that position, so bcftools merge stops with an error, as does this function by default (ref_mismatch = "error", listing the first few mismatches). With ref_mismatch = "drop" such sites are dropped; with ref_mismatch = "swap", loci whose alleles are swapped (A/C and C/A) are merged, swapping the genotypes of the later file (as rbind() does), and other mismatches are handled as with alt_mismatch. Swapping is needed e.g. for VCF files exported by PLINK 1.9, which by default set the REF allele to the major allele.

Strands are not flipped (all VCF files are on the forward strand). Loci at the same position within a file are never merged with each other (as in bcftools merge); if a file has several loci at the same position (e.g. a multiallelic site split into biallelic records, as by bcftools norm -m-), each is merged with the site of the other files that has its alleles, if any, before the others are handled as above.

The merged gen_tibble has the samples of the first file, followed by those of the second file, and so on. By default (variants = "intersection"), it keeps the sites found in all files, as rbind() does; with variants = "union", it keeps all sites (as bcftools merge), and the samples of the files without a site get missing genotypes there, or homozygous reference genotypes with missing_to_ref = TRUE (as bcftools merge -0). Sites are ordered by chromosome (in order of first appearance across the files), then by position.

Unlike gen_tibble(), by default (names_as_int = TRUE) the loci are named with integers (their index in the merged gen_tibble), rather than with their VCF IDs, to save memory with large datasets. With names_as_int = FALSE, each locus takes its name (VCF ID) from the first file where it is found (a missing ID '.' gives a name made of the chromosome and the position, as in gen_tibble()).

Sample names must be unique across files: if they are not, the function stops, unless force_samples = TRUE, in which case the duplicated names are prefixed by the index of their file, as bcftools merge --force-samples does (e.g. sample 'S3' of the second file becomes '2:S3').

As in gen_tibble(), the ploidy of each individual is estimated from the first variants of its file. The individuals of different files can have different ploidies.

See also

gt_concat_vcfs() to combine VCF files with the same samples and different loci (e.g. one file per chromosome); rbind() to merge two gen_tibble objects (e.g. read from files of other formats).

Examples

vcf_a <- system.file("extdata", "pop_a.vcf", package = "tidypopgen")
vcf_b <- system.file("extdata", "pop_b.vcf", package = "tidypopgen")
# the REF and ALT alleles of some loci are swapped between these two files
# (which a VCF from PLINK can have), so we swap them back to merge them;
# we also keep the VCF IDs as loci names (by default, unlike gen_tibble(),
# loci are named with integers to save memory)
merged_gt <- gt_merge_vcfs(c(vcf_a, vcf_b),
  ref_mismatch = "swap",
  names_as_int = FALSE,
  backingfile = tempfile("merged_")
)
#> reading the loci of /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/tidypopgen/extdata/pop_a.vcf
#> reading the loci of /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/tidypopgen/extdata/pop_b.vcf
#> merging 2 VCF files with 8 samples:
#>   20 sites (biallelic SNPs), of which 13 are in all files
#>   dropped: 5 with alleles that would make a multiallelic site, 0 with different REF alleles
#>   loci with swapped alleles: 2
#>   kept: 8 loci (intersection)
#> reading the genotypes of /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/tidypopgen/extdata/pop_a.vcf
#> reading the genotypes of /home/runner/work/_temp/Library/tidypopgen/extdata/pop_b.vcf

merged_gt
